elements.problem: The glucose rule has only (>= 11.1 AND Ketonuria). The 'with symptoms' branch fires only indirectly, when the symptom is one of the red-box items, since any of those alone already triggers the danger-signs rule. If 'symptoms' means classic hyperglycaemia symptoms (polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss, blurred vision), polyuria/weight loss/blurred vision are not on the list, and glucose >= 11.1 with those symptoms is not escalated. At minimum the branch isn't traceable in the rules.

rule_level_problems.problem: Only two of the three red-box glucose branches are explicit: < 4, and >= 11.1 + Ketonuria. The '>= 11.1 with symptoms -> 19' branch has no glucose-conditioned rule. It is covered only when the symptom is itself one of the red-box items (each already Urgent alone), not for classic hyperglycaemia symptoms such as polyuria, weight loss or blurred vision.

'Dehydration: dry mouth, poor skin turgor, BP < 90/60, pulse >= 100' is flattened into independent OR items, so a single sign (e.g. pulse >= 100, diastolic < 60, or Xerostomia) makes any diabetic Urgent. The page lists these as signs of dehydration. An (active_condition Dehydration) via a probable rule, or any2 of the signs, would follow the page more closely. Likely over-triggers for pulse >= 100 or diastolic < 60 alone.

rule_level_problems.rule: Measure waist circumference in routine diabetes care
rule_level_problems.problem: A measure task drawn from the routine-care table (outside the red box) that no rule consumes. It isn't wrong, but it is inconsistent: other routine-care measures (weight/BMI, potassium, etc.) are not encoded, and the WC targets it relates to are management aims. Harmless, but it fires on every diabetes encounter.

Pulse uses 'Pulse, function' (observable entity). It exists, but check that it is the concept VHA records pulse under (vs 'Heart rate'); if the vital is recorded under another concept the pulse >= 100 branch never fires.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: diabetes with low or high fingerprick glucose
rule_level_problems.problem: Glucose uses 'Blood glucose status' (observable entity). It is the only blood-glucose observable found, but confirm it matches how VHA records the routine glucose vital, or both glucose branches and the ketone task will never fire.

summary: The red box is well covered: all 14 urgent-attention items map to sensible SNOMED concepts under an Urgent (and DM (or …)) rule, and the < 4 and >= 11.1 + ketones glucose branches plus the ketone check task are encoded. The main gap is that 'glucose >= 11.1 with symptoms' has no explicit branch and relies on the symptom already being a red-box item. The dehydration criterion is split into single-sign triggers (pulse >= 100 or diastolic < 60 alone gives Urgent), which over-reads the page. Minor issues: an unconsumed waist-circumference measure task, and glucose/pulse observables that should be confirmed against what VHA records.
